safety_verdicts.content: Diarrhoea is associated with abdominal pain.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states diarrhea is associated with abdominal pain, but generated HPI does not explicitly document abdominal pain (only mentions no analgesia taken).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to explicitly document abdominal pain can reduce the clinician’s ability to risk-stratify acute diarrhea (e.g., considering inflammatory/infectious colitis, surgical abdomen) and may prompt additional follow-up questioning or missed escalation triggers. In this case the visit did reference abdominal pain indirectly (no analgesia taken), so the impact is mainly loss of clarity rather than a definitive harmful action.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold diagnosis is gastroenteritis; generated assessment states acute diarrhea but does not explicitly document gastroenteritis.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not labeling the assessment as “gastroenteritis” when describing it as acute diarrhea is largely a terminology/documentation gap, and it is unlikely to change immediate self-care advice, hydration guidance, or monitoring instructions in an uncomplicated presentation. The main risk is reduced diagnostic clarity for continuity of care/coding rather than direct patient harm.
